_lore:
Quarthaven is an isle of mages floating above a sea of cloud, home to four towers: the Ember Spire (fire), Tidewell Tower (water),
the Root Bastion (stone) and the Gale Loft (wind). Every mage here is born to one element and can work no other.
The elements turn in a wheel: water quenches fire, fire devours wind, wind wears down stone, stone dams water. A spell against
the element it overcomes strikes hard; against the element that overcomes it, it falls weak.
Forty days ago the Archmage Velloran vanished from the Conclave Hall and that same night the Veil, the great ward around the isle,
closed: nobody can pass it, not even by flight. The Skygate in the north stays sealed. Food from the mainland no longer comes.
Since then the four wardens (Ignatia of fire, Maelis of water, Torvald of stone, Aerin of wind) quarrel over who should take the
empty seat. The grimoire "Of the Fourfold Seal" is missing from the Library of Echoes. The Heartstone obelisk in the plaza has a
crack that grows. The old Concord forbids mages to kill one another, but nobody enforces it now. Those struck down in Quarthaven do
not stay dead: the Veil returns them, aching, to their own bed, and they remember who did it. Duels are fought with bolts, wards and
each element's own art. Mages respect skill, keep their word or lose face, and gossip about everything at the Copper Kettle.
